claims.claim: The game fails to start on Linux due to the EA launcher.

citations.review_text:
The game does not start on linux. EA drops an error without an actual error code "There's been an error", and recommends me to reset my password. At no point during the setup it ever asked me to log in, to give any data whatsoever to anywhere, so there is no password to reset, no account to manage, nothing at all. You cannot contact steam support, since its an EA game. You cannot contact EA, because its windows only, and they offer no support to other OS.
I can't give a positive, since the game can't even start starting up due to the lack of linux compatibility of the EA launcher.

The most legendary first-person shooter that's leagues better than Call of Duty and Battlefield... that nobody wants to play.

15+ minute queues in Europe. So after you're done installing the third-party EA app, editing config files and optimising the game to actually RUN... you basically get no gameplay lol.

I'd likely have left this as NO review, but making me install the buggy EA Launcher made me annoyed enough to leave a negative review. No nostalgia grace from me.

claims.claim: Reviewers report that the single-player campaign can be completed in approximately five to ten hours.

citations.review_text:
This is a good game, i cleared it in an afternoon while under blanket cover and the slowly dissipating scent of black tea which i didn't finish because i was so locked into the gameplay.

i didn't play online much but the campaign is definitely worth 5 euros.

I ended up waiting until this game was on sale becuase I've been eyeing it for a long time. I'm honestly disappointed in the story length but I don't fault it too hard due to modern gaming shifting entirely into MMO and battle royale styled games. The story is good and there is some very fun movement mechanics. I enjoyed my time playing it, but I finished the main storyline with most of the collectables on "hard" in sub 8hrs. Worth the 50% off

Level and Mechanic Design: 10/10 (The 'Cause and Effect' level is enough to go down in gaming history, perfect pilot and Titan coordination)  
Combat and Controls: 9.5/10 (Parkour is smooth, Titan punches feel impactful, gunplay feels excellent)  
Narrative and Emotional Resonance: 9.5/10 (No unnecessary dialogue, everything is in the details, BT-7274 is one of the most charming AIs in gaming history)  
Length and Replayability: 7.0/10 (6 hours straight through, but after finishing, aside from collecting everything, there’s little motivation to replay the campaign)  

In six hours, I followed Cooper and BT-7274 on Typhon, experiencing betrayal, pursuit, time travel, and life-and-death separation.  
The single-player campaign of Titanfall 2 proves that a great FPS doesn’t need to fake depth through cutscenes, nor does it need to cover up lack of gameplay with overstuffing. It just needs to perfect the fun, perfectly integrate mechanics and narrative, to create an experience that stays with you for a lifetime.  
If you’re an FPS lover, if you’ve ever been moved by Master Chief and Cortana in Halo, then you absolutely must experience Titanfall 2.  
I’m going to collect all the ‘Flight Helmets’ in the game, then watch a ‘BT First-Person’ ending montage on TikTok. Also, EA, I’m begging you, please release Titanfall 3 soon, my wallet is ready!

That was probably the first time when I didn't expect the game to end so quickly. 
The only thing that I can say about the campaign - it was short, but great. It took only about 5 hours to complete it. 
There's something special about this product and its setting and history - something that Apex Legends lacks the most.
It's sad to see what the series has turned into with all these inclusive characters with no story and development, a ton of skins and vibrant visuals.
[b] In conclusion, I would strongly recommend giving it a go [/b]

claims.claim: The single-player campaign is relatively short.

citations.review_text: I'll forever sing the praises of this game. Everything from the sound design, movement, and gunplay has insane attention to detail and continues to rival that of newer shooters. It was made by people who left Activision to make a better game than COD, and it feels that way. Its core gameplay is unique and well-made; its campaign is a blast (though short); and everything is snappy, responsive, and satisfying. It's a shame the player base and devs have abandoned it for Apex. I wish they'd make a third.

My expectations for Titanfall 2 were very high, and I am happy to say that this game didn't disappoint me in the slightest.

In terms of gameplay, Titanfall is a first person shooter where you can either play as the Pilot or as a Titan; in the first case, your movement is very important: double jump, wall running, sliding... Mastering the movement is a really ambitious and difficult endeavor, but even with the basics moving is satisfying.
Overall, the guns are fun to use and pretty well designed, even if I find a few of them kind of lacking.
Meanwhile, as a Titan, the gameplay becomes "heavier"; movement is still important, but the game does a great job at making you feel incredibly powerful in a different way. The different Titan loadouts feel fairly balanced and enjoyable.

The campaign, while quite short (around 6 hours), has left quite an impression on me; the story is basic, but even still, it manages to make the characters (even if some appear just briefly) likeable, and the ending is fantastic. But the best thing of the campaign is definitely the level design: EVERY SINGLE level is exceptional and feels unique in its own way.

Getting into the multiplayer today is very difficult, unfortunatly the remaining playerbase is very small, and sometimes even finding matches can take a long time: most gamemodes are pretty much impossible to play; but I still had some fun while playing.

claims.claim: Finding active multiplayer matches can take time due to a small player base and regional queue issues.

citations.review_text:
So let me preface this review with a clarification: these hours at the time of review are my PC hours on this game. I have been playing the online attrition in this game since day 1, and have played on PS4, XBOX One, and returned to PC, playing a couple matches off and on. I was here in the golden days of initial launch to the DDOS attacks in 2021 (you can google it, don't feel like opening that can of worms here) and hopping from server to server during that whole s**t-show just trying to find games after work. 

     So, getting that out of the way, do I recommend the game still? Yes, it has it's flaws, mainly latency. It is not constant, but when you see another player that looks like they are using instant transmission that appears right in front of you with a fist in your mouth, it's a bit obnoxious and it happens from time to time, but you finish the match and move on. Its definitely not like its prime in those first 5 years, but there is a community that bounced back still keeping this game alive. You can find games (it may take a bit of time to queue initially but once you're in the rotation, you will get games pretty consistently) And when you get into your groove, your controls are dialed in, and you're just moving, you can feel some of that magic still shining through.

   Movement is awesome, customization to how you want to play is great, maps are pretty good, all the bones are still there and they are good bones for a great experience. A good, honest, not very toxic online experience. I am heavily biased to attrition, but there are plenty of other modes, and even co-op in Frontier Defense. We may never get Titanfall 3, but even if we do it's still a good time to get into a good online shooter experience.

Oh right, obviously the campaign is great. but you can see other reviews and articles about that.

claims.claim: Reviewers report that the campaign features a strong story and characters, though it leaves them wanting more content.

citations.review_text:
Titanfall 2 may well be my favorite game of all time. That's hard to say definitively, but for sure, it's top 3.
Of all time.
The movement, gunplay, Titans, loadout customization, art, lore, characters... It's just so good!

AND THE CAMPAIGN. Oh my god, the campaign. literally the only negative thing I can say about the campaign is that I want more. I miss Jack and BT, man.

All in all, the only bad things I can say about this game, is that it needed a longer campaign, and I need more hours in it. 144 (at time of writing) is not nearly enough. I wish I could click the recommend button twice.
Please play this game,
Especially if you're coming from something like EMPULSE, you're gonna love this.

Hey. Hey c'mere. Listen.

I know the servers have been down for a while and everyone forgot about this game. But not you. And not me either. Now they don't want you to know this, but if you don't want to mess with the private servers, and the modding, and all that nonsense... just don't; you don't have to.

The campaign is the best campaign I've played in a video game. Period. No strings. I would have paid double what I did for the campaign alone. 

Have you ever wondered what sex is like? It's Titanfall 2.

Have you ever wondered what the meaning of life is? Also Titanfall 2.

Have you ever wondered what it would feel like to take hard drugs via your eyeballs, like a photosynthesizing meth addict? I'm gonna stop you right there, because you already know.

Titanfall 2 all day, baby.

claims.claim: Reviewers describe the single-player campaign as story-rich with a good narrative and high replay value.

citations.review_text: Literally one of the best games ive ever played. No matter how many years after release with zero updates, every single fight no matter titan or pilot feels cinematic. Every core aspect blends into each other perfectly. 100% reccomend for everyone, the campagin is story rich and the multiplayer is on its level which is insanely high.

A game ahead of its time. Gameplay, graphics and story still has replay value to this day. Not to add still thriving multiplayer community presence. If you're looking for a mech game made with care, look no further.

P.S. A must have Steam Deck title.
